focus-management.evidence: The email input is DOM index 0 among focusable elements (after the tabindex=-1 logo link), but the global tab walk's first stop is the Continue button (submit input). The local walk confirms: targetIndexInFocusables=0 but stopsToReach=8 — the driver had to tab through all 9 other focusable elements (wrapping around) before the email input became active. This is a focus-order defect: the primary data-entry field is skipped on the first Tab press, placing users at the submit button instead. 2.4.3 Focus Order.

dynamic-announcement.evidence: When the email input is finally reached by keyboard (after wrapping), the vsrAnnouncement is 'assertive: Invalid email address'. This assertive announcement fires without user submitting anything — an error message announcing on mere focus arrival. Pre-populated alert regions in the DOM (role=alert with text 'Invalid email address', 'Invalid mobile number', 'Enter your mobile number or email' all display:none but with content already present). An assertive announcement that wasn't triggered by a user action is disruptive. Additionally, the email field has no aria-describedby linking it to the error message region — error association is missing even though alerts exist.

forms-instructions-errors.evidence: Error identification issues: (1) The form's drive.forms[0] shows ariaInvalidSet=false after submit — aria-invalid is never set on the email field when invalid, so the error state is not programmatically identified per 3.3.1. (2) No aria-describedby on the email input linking it to the visible error alert — errors appear in role=alert regions but are not associated with the specific field. (3) nativeValidationOnly=true — the form relies solely on native browser validation, which does not meet 3.3.1 requirements for custom error identification with suggestions. The email field also has required=false and aria-required=null despite being required — omitting required state from programmatic exposure (also 3.3.2/4.1.2 gap).
